display: Abraham Lincoln was born February 12, 1809, near what is now Hodgenville, Kentucky.
Lincoln was mortally wounded at Ford’s Theatre on the night of April 14, 1865, and died at the Petersen House at 7:22 a.m. on April 15, 1865, aged 56.
In 1859 Lincoln described himself as "six feet, four inches, nearly" in height.
In his tenth year Lincoln was kicked by a horse and, in his own account, "apparently killed for a time."
On January 23, 1841, Lincoln wrote to John T. Stuart, "I am now the most miserable man living."
Lincoln’s recurrent melancholy is retrospectively interpreted by modern clinicians as chronic depression that did not prevent him from leading the nation.
Lincoln’s mother, Nancy Hanks Lincoln, died of milk sickness on October 5, 1818, when he was nine.

Marfan syndrome, or another inherited marfanoid disorder such as multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B, has been proposed retrospectively from Lincoln’s build; the diagnosis is disputed and has never been genetically confirmed.
Lincoln’s older sister, Sarah Lincoln Grigsby, died on January 20, 1828, at age twenty-one, from complications during delivery that also took her infant’s life.
Lincoln’s son Edward ("Eddie") died on February 1, 1850, after a long illness, at three years and ten months.
Lincoln’s son William ("Willie") died in the White House on February 20, 1862, probably of typhoid fever, at age eleven.

Lincoln’s November 1863 illness after the Gettysburg Address has been retrospectively interpreted as unmodified smallpox, more serious than his physicians reported publicly; the interpretation is disputed.
